summary: Carlo Giussani worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at the Scuola Normale Superiore, Pisa, and Turin, and under Giuseppe Bardelli, Albrecht Weber, Rudolf von Roth, Friedrich von Spiegel, and Graziadio Isaia Ascoli. He taught at Liceo Daniele Manin and Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano.
Carlo Jamelle Harris is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts in Philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin (attested 2009).

Carlo Puini was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Pisa. In 1877, he became extraordinary Professor of East Asian history and geography at the University of Florence.

Linguist Carlo Salvioni studied at the University of Basel and completed his PhD at Leipzig under Karl Brugmann. He held posts at the universities of Turin, Milan, and Pavia, and at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano beginning in 1902.

Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Carlos Garcia-Jane studied at the universities of Barcelona, Aberystwyth, South Wales, and Edinburgh. He served as bibliographer at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies, librarian at the Royal Central School, and reviews editor for Buddhist Studies Review.

Carmen Blacker was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied at SOAS, Somerville College, and Keio University under Shigeru Gorai. She served as Lecturer in Japanese at the University of Cambridge and president of the Folklore Society (1982–1984).

Carmen Dragonetti worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy after studying at the National University of San Marcos. She was a professor at the University of Buenos Aires and served as vice director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2018).

Carmen Meinert is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who earned her PhD at the University of Bonn. She worked as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008) and joined Ruhr University Bochum's CERES in 2013.
Carol A. Breckenridge was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1968 to 1976 and held a post at the University of Chicago.

Carol S. Anderson specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under John A. Brinkman and W. S. Karunatillake, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College (attested 2004).

Carola Roloff works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Geshe Thubten Ngawang and completed her doctorate at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson, later serving there as a lecturer and visiting professor, alongside posts at CIHTS and Oslo.
Carola S. Carstens specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Rice University from 1998 to 1999 and completed her doctorate at the University of Hamburg in 2006.
Carole M. Cusack is a religious studies scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Sydney (1988–1995). She became Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Sydney in 2013.

Tibetologist and anthropologist Carole McGranahan studied at Colgate University and completed her PhD at the University of Michigan under Nicholas Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler. Around 2001, she joined the University of Colorado Boulder, serving as Assistant Professor of Anthropology until ~2008.

Caroline Humphrey is a scholar of religious studies and Central Asian studies. She studied at Girton College, Cambridge, and Leeds, completing her PhD under Edmund Leach. She held posts at the Scott Polar Research Institute and University of Cambridge (1978–2010).

Caroline Rhys Davids worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, studying at UCL under George Croom Robertson, T. W. Rhys Davids, and Reinhold Rost. She lectured at Owens College/Manchester and SOAS, and was General Editor of the Pali Text Society (1907–1942).

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed PhD degrees at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington and at Wichita State University, later serving as Director at the University of Kansas in 2017.
Carson T. Schütze is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1997.

Carsten Colpe was a scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied under Hans Heinrich Schaeder (~1948–1954). He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1962–1969) and the Free University of Berlin (~1969–1997).

Caterina Conio worked in Indology and philosophy, studying at Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore, the University of Florence, Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti, and with Paul Hacker. In 1974, she taught Indian religion and philosophy at Pisa.
